item.title: AI Could Be as Good as Electricity, Says Opinion's Schrager
item.description: Allison Schrager, Bloomberg Opinion columnist, says AI could lead to sustained economic growth, possibly for the next 100 years. She speaks during a Bloomberg Opinion event held exclusively for Bloomberg.com subscribers in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Putin Releases Hostage, Earns US Praise as Humanitarian
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Jim Gilmore, former Virginia governor, RNC chair and ambassador to the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe, says the US has made a dramatic reversal in its policy toward Ukraine and argues Americans deserve an explanation for the shift. Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA) says she would “100%” support Representative Thomas Massie's resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and says he would be “on the hot seat” when lawmakers return to Washington after the midterms. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: What Happens If Democrats Control Congress?
item.description: Timothy L. O'Brien, senior executive editor for Bloomberg Opinion and Bloomberg Opinion Columnist Ronald Brownstein talk about what could happen if Democrats take back control of Congress. They speak during a Bloomberg Opinion event held exclusively for Bloomberg.com subscribers in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Our Politics Are Becoming More Parliamentary, Says Opinion's Brownstein
item.description: Bloomberg Opinion Columnist Ronald Brownstein says our politics are becoming more polarized and are becoming more parliamentary. He talks about what voters are looking for during a Bloomberg Opinion event held exclusively for Bloomberg.com subscribers in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: There Certainly Is an AI Bubble, Says Opinion's Authers
item.description: Bloomberg Opinion Columnist John Authers says there is an AI bubble and someone is going to "lose their shirt" because of it. He speaks during a Bloomberg Opinion event held exclusively for Bloomberg.com subscribers in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Can't Wish Away Inflation, O'Brien Says
item.description: Timothy L. O'Brien, senior executive editor for Bloomberg Opinion, says President Donald Trump can't wish away the inflation problem. He speaks during a Bloomberg Opinion event held exclusively for Bloomberg.com subscribers in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Kamlager-Dove Says She Would Back Hegseth Impeachment
item.description: Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA) says she would “100%” support Representative Thomas Massie's resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and says he would be “on the hot seat” when lawmakers return to Washington after the midterms. Rep. Kamlager-Dove also says she is confident in Los Angeles County's election safeguards after touring its ballot-processing facility and says inactive or canceled registrants identified in records provided by the Justice Department did not receive ballots. She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: Make Your Move Summit (Podcast)
item.description:
US small business optimism fell to a three-month low in September as economic expectations dimmed and a smaller share of firms indicated it was a good time to expand. The net share of owners who expect business conditions to improve declined 4 percentage points to a four-month low of 6%. Despite a falling economic sentiment, JPMorganChase says most small business owners view their own business outlook in a positive light, highlighting the resiliency of small businesses. Bloomberg Businessweek is live from the Chase Make Your Move Summit in Atlanta discussing the future of small businesses in America.
On today's episode:
Stevie Baron, CEO Chase for Business Katie Kirkpatrick, President & CEO of the Metro Atlanta Chamber Leslie Wims Morris, CEO, Chase Auto Reggie Washington, Restaurateur at SONAT Hospitality Group & Southern National Restaurant (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: EU Nears Market Securitization Reform in Bid to Unleash Billions
item.description: The European Union reached a provisional agreement to overhaul rules governing the bloc’s securitizations markets, a deal that would unleash billions of euros to finance initiatives in key areas such as defense and climate resilience.
item.dc:creator: Esteban Duarte and Laura Noonan

item.title: Gilmore: US Has Made a ‘180 Degree’ Shift on Ukraine
item.description: Jim Gilmore, former Virginia governor, RNC chair and ambassador to the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe, says the US has made a dramatic reversal in its policy toward Ukraine and argues Americans deserve an explanation for the shift. Gilmore calls Russian President Vladimir Putin a war criminal, rejecting special envoy Steve Witkoff's characterization of Putin as a humanitarian, and says the US should continue standing behind Ukraine. He also says a plan involving Russian diesel and oil would put money into Russian pockets. He speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Senate Race in Deep Red Mississippi Is Getting Trump’s Attention
item.description: A US Senate contest in the historically Republican state of Mississippi is drawing fresh attention in the final stretch of the midterm election cycle, with President Donald Trump planning a rally to boost the GOP candidate and control of the chamber hanging on the outcome of races in states the president won two years ago.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove and Bill Faries

item.title: El-Sayed's Final Test in Michigan Is Here
item.description: Bloomberg Opinion's Nia-Malika Henderson joined the show to discuss the final debate in Michigan's closely contested Senate race. She speaks with Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UK Chancellor to Court Entrepreneurs with Cuts to Regulation
item.description: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey will aim his first budget later this month at “bloody-minded entrepreneurs” by cutting the cost of business, he said in an interview.
item.dc:creator: Lucy White

item.title: New Zealand Inflation Slows Ahead of Year-End Fuel Spike
item.description: New Zealand’s annual inflation slowed more than expected in the third quarter as fuel prices retreated, offering a brief respite to the government little more than two weeks from an election.
item.dc:creator: Tracy Withers

item.title: CME Group CEO Terry Duffy on Earnings, 24/7 Energy Contracts and Managing Risk
item.description: CME Group Chairman and CEO Terry Duffy said elevated trading activity reflects persistent, not merely short-term, uncertainty. He pointed to geopolitical tensions, including conflict in the Middle East and a reported oil-field strike that quickly drove prices higher, and warned of inflationary effects. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Texas Camp Hit by Floods Must Have New Manager, Judge Says
item.description: Camp Mystic, the Texas girls camp where 28 people were killed in flash floods last summer, must have a new management team with the power to settle lawsuits filed against the company, replacing the family blamed for the deaths, a judge ruled.
item.dc:creator: Steven Church

item.title: Bolsonaro to Unleash Petrobras Without Privatizing, Adviser Says
item.description: If Flávio Bolsonaro wins Brazil’s presidential runoff on Oct. 25, he will give the nation’s state oil company broad freedom to reshape its portfolio while seeking to bring more private investment into sectors dominated by the state-controlled oil producer, according to one of his energy advisers.
item.dc:creator: Mariana Durao

item.title: Meta Offers Zuckerberg New Shares to Keep Him in California
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. signed an agreement with Mark Zuckerberg to keep him living in the same jurisdiction as the company’s headquarters after the CEO said he was weighing leaving California if the state passes a wealth tax.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Marques and Ed Ludlow

item.title: Elon Musk’s Texas Senate Race Donations Play Into James Talarico’s Hand
item.description: Elon Musk’s move to spend millions of dollars to support Republican Ken Paxton in his US Senate race is opening up a potent line of attack about money in politics from Democratic challenger James Talarico.
item.dc:creator: Dana Hull, Bill Allison and Joe Lovinger

item.title: US Fuel Sellers Warn on Prices Over Potential Pipeline Shift
item.description: US fuel retailers and marketers are warning that consumers face higher energy prices if a federal regulator approves a plan that would let oil pipeline operators freely negotiate fees with their customers.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Elkin, Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Naureen S. Malik
